items.title: Corollary 3.34: $C^k$ on $k$-dependent neighbourhoods

book.label: §3.3, Corollary 3.34, p. 88
book.statement: If the sc$^0$-contraction germ $f$ is sc-smooth, then for all $m, k \ge 0$ there is a relatively open $V_{m,k} \ni 0$ in $\widetilde C$ with (1) $\delta(V_{m,k}) \subseteq W_m$, (2) $\delta : V_{m,k} \to W_m$ of class $C^k$. In particular $\delta$ is sc-smooth at the smooth point $0$.

lean.statement: If $B$ is an sc-smooth germ, then for every $m$ and $k$ there is a relatively open $V \ni 0$ in $\widetilde C$ (namely $N(m+k+s) \cap \widetilde C$) with $\delta(V) \subseteq W_m$ and the level-$m$ map of $\delta$ of class $C^k$ on $V$. The last sentence on one germ: the solution germ is an sc-smooth germ (sc$^k$ for every $k$ on the same sequence of sets) on a diagonal germ $V_m = N(m + t_m) \cap \widetilde C$, $t_m = \sum_{j \le m} s_j$, and a solution germ there.

diff: As in the text, with $V_{m,k}$ depending on $k$. The last sentence holds on one germ: sc$^j$ involves only the levels $\ge j$ of a germ (`isSckGerm_of_levels`), so the $k$-dependent germs $\mathrm{germ}(s_k)$ of Theorem 3.33 can be replaced by one diagonal germ, which shrinks fast with the level ($t_m = 2^{m+1} - m - 2$ for $s_k = 2^k - 1$) but is a germ of neighbourhoods (Findings, Chapter 3, item 250; formerly “in this sense only”, updated in the third addendum of this page). The citation \"Proposition 3.40\" should be Theorem 3.40, and it is not needed *(book 2017: unchanged, renumbered: "Proposition 3.11" for Theorem 3.11, p. 79)* (Findings, Chapter 3, item 8).

items.title: Theorem 3.35: the germ implicit function theorem on a partial quadrant

book.label: §3.3, Theorem 3.35, p. 89
book.statement: Let $\widetilde C$ be a finite-dimensional partial quadrant in $\mathbb R^n$. An sc$^0$-contraction germ of class sc$^k$ has a solution germ of class sc$^k$; if $f$ is sc-smooth so is its solution germ.

lean.statement: For $\widetilde C$ a partial quadrant in a finite-dimensional $P$: if $B$ is sc$^k$ there is $s$ with $\delta$ sc$^k$ on $\mathrm{germ}(s)$; if $B$ is sc-smooth, $\delta$ is an sc-smooth germ (sc$^k$ for every $k$) on **one** germ $N(m + t_m) \cap \widetilde C$ (earlier form: for every $k$ an $s$ with $\delta$ sc$^k$ on $\mathrm{germ}(s)$). In the text's form: for an sc$^0$-contraction germ $f = w - B(a, w)$ of Definition 3.28 on a quadrant-like $\widetilde C$ and **any** representative $(V, \delta)$ of its solution germ ($\delta$ sc$^0$, $\delta(0) = 0$, $f(a, \delta(a)) = 0$ on $V_0$): if $f$ is sc$^k$, $\delta$ is sc$^k$ on a germ $V' \subseteq V$; if $f$ is sc-smooth, $\delta$ is an sc-smooth germ on one germ $V' \subseteq V$.

diff: The last sentence is proved as `IsScSmoothGerm` on one germ (the diagonal germ of V3.31); before the third addendum of this page only for every $k$ on a germ depending on $k$ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 2, 250).

In the text's form the hypotheses are on $f$ ($f$ is sc$^k$ iff $B$ is, `isSckGerm_contractionMap_iff`) and any representative of the solution germ is allowed (it agrees with the constructed one near $0$, by the uniqueness of Theorem 3.29); the conclusion holds on a smaller germ $V' \subseteq V$, as for Theorem 3.33 (V3.30), and $\mathbb R^n$ is generalized to a quadrant-like $\widetilde C$ in a finite-dimensional $P$ (Findings, Chapter 3, item 251). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Definition 3.37: the basic class

book.label: §3.4, Definition 3.37, p. 90
book.statement: A basic germ $f : \mathcal O([0, \infty)^k \oplus \mathbb R^{n-k} \oplus W, 0) \to (\mathbb R^N \oplus W, 0)$ is an sc-smooth germ such that $P_W \circ f$ is an sc$^0$-contraction germ; $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{basic}}$ is the class of basic germs.

lean.statement: Definition 3.7 restated: `IsBasicGerm` (V3.10).

diff: Same notion as Definition 3.7.

items.title: Theorem 3.38: weak stability of basic germs

book.label: §3.4, Theorem 3.38, p. 90 (proof pp. 90–93)
book.statement: For a basic germ $f$ and the principal part $s$ of an sc$^+$-section with $s(0) = 0$ there is a strong bundle isomorphism $\Phi : U \triangleleft (\mathbb R^N \oplus W) \to U' \triangleleft (\mathbb R^{N'} \oplus W')$ covering an sc-diffeomorphism $\varphi$ such that $(\Phi_*(f + s))^1$ (levels raised by one) is a basic germ; $n - N = n' - N'$.

lean.statement: Given $f$ basic with contraction $B$ and the data `StabilityData` (the $W$-component $s$ of the sc$^+$-germ, $s(0) = 0$, and an sc-Fredholm splitting $W = C \oplus X = R \oplus Z$ of $1 + D_2s(0)$, which exists by Proposition 1.10): with the **linear** base change $\psi(a, w) = ((a, (1 - P_1)w), P_1w)$ and fibre change $\Psi(q, w) = ((q, (1 - P_2)w), L^{-1}P_2w)$, the germ $(\Phi_*(f + s))^1 = \Psi \circ (f + s)^1 \circ \psi^{-1}$ on $\psi(U_{m+1})$ is a basic germ with contraction $\hat B = L^{-1}P_2(B - S)$; zeros correspond under $\psi$; and $\dim C = \dim Z$.

diff: The coordinate change is linear, so a pair of sc-isomorphisms replaces a general strong bundle isomorphism; the text's $\tau : Z \to C$ is not applied (new target $(Q \oplus Z) \oplus X^1$). The index raise is a change of sc-structure (Proposition 1.17 for germs) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 60–61).

\"$S$ is an arbitrarily small contraction on every level $m \ge 1$\" needs the operator-norm continuity of the derivative of $s$ on level $m + 1$ and the mean value inequality (item 62). Only the $W$-component of $s$ enters; $B$ is used only through Definition 3.7 (item 63).
The linear coordinate change is a strong bundle isomorphism of the index-raised structures (`StabilityData.linIso_isStrongBundleIso`, V3.76).

items.title: Theorem 3.40: local regularity and compactness

book.label: §3.5, Theorem 3.40, p. 94 (proof pp. 95–98)
book.statement: Let $f = h + s : U \to \mathbb R^N \oplus W$, $h$ a basic germ, $s$ an sc$^+$-germ with $s(0) = 0$, $S = \{f = 0\}$. There are relatively open neighbourhoods $U \supset O(0) \supset O(1) \supset \cdots$ of $0$ on level $0$ with $\mathrm{cl}_{C_0}(S \cap O(m)) \subseteq C_m$.

lean.statement: Let $B$ be an sc$^0$-contraction germ on $\widetilde C \oplus W$ with **$\widetilde C$ closed**, $\mathbf s$ sc$^0$ into $W^1$ with $\mathbf s(0) = 0$, and $S$ any set of solutions of $w = B(a, w) - \mathbf s(a, w)$ in $U_0$. There are nested open $O(i) \ni 0$ in $E_0$ with $\mathrm{cl}_{E_0}(S \cap O(i)) = \iota_i(K_i)$ for compact $K_i \subseteq E_i$; in particular $\mathrm{cl}(S \cap O(i)) \subseteq E_i$. For a basic germ plus an sc$^+$-germ this gives the local Theorem 3.12.

diff: Stronger: the closures are compact in $E_i$, which Theorem 3.12 needs and Theorem 3.40 does not state (Findings, Chapter 3, item 12). Weaker hypotheses: of $f$ only the $W$-component, with $B$ sc$^0$ and the contraction estimate, and $\mathbf s$ sc$^0$ into $W^1$ (item 14).

**$\widetilde C$ closed** is a hypothesis because the theorem is proved for convex $\widetilde C$; it holds for partial quadrants. The induction left to the reader needs existence, bound and continuity of the lifts together (item 13); the $O(i)$ are one level ahead of the text's.

items.title: Corollary 3.41: the linearization at nearby solutions

book.label: §3.5, Corollary 3.41, p. 98 (proof pp. 98–100)
book.statement: For $f = h + s : U \to \mathbb R^N \oplus W$, $h$ basic, $s$ an sc$^+$-map, $s(0) = 0$, $Df(0)$ surjective: there is $U' \subseteq U$ relatively open on level $0$ such that (1) solutions in $U'$ are on level $1$; (2) at such solutions $Df(a, w) : E \to F$ is a surjective Fredholm operator of index $n - N$.

lean.statement: For the data of Theorem 3.38 ($f := h$ basic, $s$ the $W$-component of the sc$^+$-germ) with $D(h + s)(0)$ surjective: there is $r > 0$ such that every zero $x$ of $h + s$ in $U_0$ with $|x|_0 < r$ is $\iota(x_1)$ with $x_1 \in U_1$, and $D(h + s)(x_1) : E_0 \to F_0$ is a surjective Fredholm operator of index $\dim P - \dim Q$.

diff: The $\mathbb R^N$-component of the sc$^+$-map is absorbed into $h$ (as in Theorem 3.54, Findings item 85). The Fredholm property with index holds at every $x \in U_1$ small on level $1$, not only at solutions; $Df(x) = Df(0) + S(x) + K(x)$ with $\|S(x)\| \le \varepsilon$ and $K(x)$ compact; surjectivity from $\dim\ker \le n - N = \mathrm{ind}$; the detour through level $2$ is not needed (item 71).

items.title: Lemma 3.42: solutions of the push-forward are on level 1

book.label: §3.5, Lemma 3.42, p. 101
book.statement: (In the setting after Theorem 3.38, $g = \Phi_*f$, $\delta$ the solution germ of $P' \circ g^1$.) There are $\varepsilon'_0, \tau'_0$ such that a solution $(a', w')$ of $g = 0$ with $|a'|_0 \le \varepsilon'_0$, $|w'|_0 \le \tau'_0$ has $w' = \delta(a')$, and $|\delta(a')|_0 \le \tau'_0$ if $|a'|_0 \le \varepsilon'_0$.

lean.statement: For every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $r > 0$ such that every zero $x'$ of $g = \Phi_*(f + s)$ in $\psi(U)$ with $|x'|_0 < r$ has its $X$-component on level $1$ with $|\cdot|_1 < \varepsilon$.

diff: The formal statement is the regularity Theorem 3.43's proof uses (solutions near $0$ lie on level $1$ and are small there), proved from the lifts of Theorem 3.40 and the linearity of $\psi$; the identification $w' = \delta(a')$ is made inside Theorem 3.43 (Findings, Chapter 3, item 65).

items.title: Theorem 3.43: local germ-solvability I

book.label: §3.5, Theorem 3.43, p. 102 (proof pp. 102–106)
book.statement: Let $f = h + s$ with $Df(0)$ surjective and $K = \ker Df(0)$ in good position to $C$, $g = \Phi_*(f)$. Then $K' = \ker Dg(0)$ is in good position to $C'$, there are a good complement $Y'$ and a $C^1$ map $\tau : V \to Y'_1$, $V$ relatively open in $K' \cap C'$, with (1) $\tau$ an sc-smooth germ; (2) $\tau(0) = 0$, $D\tau(0) = 0$; (3) after shrinking $U$, $\varphi(\{f = 0\}) = \{g = 0\} = \{y + \tau(y) \mid y \in V\}$.

lean.statement: For an sc-smooth germ $g$ with $g(0) = 0$ whose index-raised germ $g^1$ is basic (`ShiftedBasicData`), $\widetilde C$ a partial quadrant, $Dg(0)$ onto, $K' = \ker Dg(0)$ in good position, and the regularity hypothesis of Lemma 3.42: there are a good complement $Y = Z \oplus W$, $V$ relatively open in $K' \cap C'$ and $\tau : V \to Y$ of class $C^1$ with values on level $1$, $\tau(0) = 0$, $D\tau(0) = 0$, every $y + \tau(y)$ a zero in $U$, every zero in $U$ near $0$ of this form; and (1) for every $k \ge 1$ a relatively open $V_k \subseteq V$ containing $0$ and a $C^k$ map $\tau_k : V_k \to E_k$ with $\iota_k\tau_k = \tau$ on $V_k$.

diff: (1), \"$\tau$ is an sc-smooth germ\", is proved level-wise with $k$-dependent neighbourhoods (the reading of V3.22 and Corollary 3.34): $C^k$ into $E_k$ on $V_k$. The proof applies Theorem 3.78 to $H$ at regularity $k$ and identifies its solution with the $C^1$ one by the uniqueness clause, which the text does not discuss (Findings, Chapter 3, item 70). `theorem_3_43` is the statement without (1). Lemma 3.42 enters as the explicit hypothesis `hreg`, proved for the push-forward of Theorem 3.38 in V3.37 (item 65).

A gap in the text's proof of (3) is filled: the $\widetilde K$-component of a solution lies in $\widetilde C$, because $|z| \le \varepsilon|k|$ near $0$ (item 66). $H$ is $C^j$ near $0$ by Corollary 3.34 for $g^1$ and Proposition 1.18 for germs (item 67).
With the good complement closed and its projection onto $K'$ mapping $\widetilde C \oplus W$ into itself: V3.77.

items.title: Lemma 3.44: the kernel of $Dg(0)$ is a graph

book.label: §3.5, Lemma 3.44, p. 103
book.statement: The map $\alpha \mapsto (\alpha, D\delta(0)\alpha)$ induces a linear isomorphism $\widetilde K = \ker DH(0) \to \ker Dg(0) = K'$, $H(a) = (1 - P') \circ g(a, \delta(a))$.

lean.statement: In the data of Theorem 3.43: $\ker Dg(0) = \{(\alpha, D\delta(0)\alpha) \mid \alpha \in \ker DH(0)\}$; the $W$-component of $Dg(0)(0, \zeta)$ is $\zeta$ for every $\zeta \in W_0$; and $DH(0)$ is onto when $Dg(0)$ is.

diff: \"Recalling from Lemma 3.9 that $D_2B(0) = 0$\": Lemma 3.9 gives it for $g^1$ on level $1$; the level-$0$ identity follows by density of $W_1$ in $W_0$ (Findings, Chapter 3, item 68).

items.title: Lemma 3.45: good position under linear isomorphisms

book.label: §3.5, Lemma 3.45, p. 104
book.statement: The complement $(K')^\perp = T\varphi(0)(K^\perp)$ is a good complement of $K' = T\varphi(0)K$ in $E'$.

lean.statement: For any continuous linear isomorphism $S : E_0 \to E'_0$ with $x \in C \iff Sx \in C'$: $S$ carries a good complement $P$ of $N$ to a good complement $S(P)$ of $S(N)$, with $\varepsilon' = \varepsilon/(\|S\|\|S^{-1}\| + 1)$, and good position to good position.

diff: Stated for any linear isomorphism carrying $C$ onto $C'$ (Findings, Chapter 3, item 21); since the coordinate change of Theorem 3.38 is linear, this is the form used.

items.title: Lemma 3.46: good position of $\ker DH(0)$

book.label: §3.5, Lemma 3.46, p. 104 (proof §3.8.2, pp. 129–132)
book.statement: $\widetilde K = \ker DH(0) \subseteq \mathbb R^{n'}$ is in good position to $\widetilde C$, and there is a good complement $Z$ of $\widetilde K$ in $\mathbb R^{n'}$ such that $Z \oplus W'$ is a good complement of $K' = \ker Dg(0)$.

lean.statement: If $K' = \{(\alpha, L\alpha) \mid \alpha \in \widetilde K\}$ has the good complement $Y'$ with respect to $\widetilde C \oplus W$, there is a good complement $Z$ of $\widetilde K$ with respect to $\widetilde C$ such that $Z \times W$ is a good complement of $K'$; and if $K'$ is in good position, so is $\widetilde K$.

diff: The proof takes $Z' = \mathrm{pr}(Y')$ and a right inverse of the projection; the text's intermediate complement $Y_0$ is not needed (Findings, Chapter 3, item 64).

items.title: Corollary 3.47: local germ-solvability for $f + s$

book.label: §3.5, Corollary 3.47, p. 106 (proof pp. 106–108)
book.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 3.43 there are a good complement $Y$ of $K$ and a $C^1$ map $\sigma : V \to Y_1$, $V$ relatively open in $K \cap C$, with (1) $\sigma$ an sc-smooth germ; (2) $\sigma(0) = 0$, $D\sigma(0) = 0$; (3) $\{x \in U \mid f(x) = 0\} = \{v + \sigma(v) \mid v \in V\}$ after shrinking $U$.

lean.statement: For a basic germ $f$ and the data of Theorem 3.38 with $D(f + s)(0)$ surjective and kernel $K$ in good position to $\widetilde C \oplus W$: a good complement $Y$ of $K$, $V$ relatively open in $K \cap C$, $\sigma : V \to Y$ of class $C^1$ with values on level $1$, $\sigma(0) = 0$, $D\sigma(0) = 0$, every $v + \sigma(v)$ a zero of $f + s$ in $U_0$, an open $U'' \ni 0$ in which every zero is of this form; and (1) for every $k \ge 1$ a relatively open $V_k \subseteq V$ containing $0$ and a $C^k$ lift $\sigma_k : V_k \to E_k$ of $\sigma$.

diff: (1) in the level-wise sense of V3.38 (Findings, Chapter 3, item 70); `theorem_3_47` is the statement without (1), the form Theorem 3.54 uses so far.

Because $\psi$ is linear, the transport back is linear algebra ($K = \psi^{-1}(K')$, $Y = \psi^{-1}(Y')$, $\sigma = \psi^{-1}\tau\psi$); the text's degeneracy-index argument with Lemma 3.70 and Theorem 3.72 is not needed (item 69).
With the good complement closed and its projection onto $K$ mapping $\widetilde C \oplus W$ into itself: V3.77.

book.statement: Definition 3.4 restated for a tame strong local bundle $K \to O$.

items.title: Definitions 3.50 and 3.51: sc-Fredholm germs and sections of a tame strong bundle (restated)

items.title: Proposition 3.52: the linearization at a zero is Fredholm of index $n - N$

book.label: §3.6, Proposition 3.52, p. 110
book.statement: If $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section of the tame strong bundle $P : Y \to X$ and $f(x) = 0$, then $Tf(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ is an sc-Fredholm operator (of the index $n - N$ of the basic germ, as the proof of Theorem 3.54 uses).

lean.statement: For a section $f$ with $(f, x_0)$ an sc-Fredholm germ and $f(x_0) = 0$: in the chart of Definition 3.11 centred at $x_0$, with the filling germ $g$ (a derivative family $Dg$ on a germ $G \subseteq U$) and the local sc$^+$-germ $s$, $Dg(0) : E \to F$ is an sc-Fredholm operator, $T_0O = Dr(0)E$ and $K_0 = \rho(0)F$ are sc-subspaces, and $Tf(x_0) = Dg(0)|_{T_0O} : T_0O \to K_0$ is an sc-Fredholm operator; for **every** conjugation of $g - s$ to a basic germ $h : O(\widetilde C \oplus W, 0) \to \mathbb R^N \oplus W$, $\widetilde C \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ (`ConjugationData`), both are Fredholm of index $n - N$ on every level. In particular $n - N$ does not depend on the conjugation. For an sc-Fredholm section the same holds in **every** strong bundle chart around a zero $y$: at the point $z$ over $y$, $T_zO = Dr(z)E$ and $K_z = \rho(z)F$ are sc-subspaces and $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z$ is sc-Fredholm, of index $n - N$ on every level.

diff: Proved in sc form, in charts: $T_0O$, $K_0$ (and $T_zO$, $K_z$ in any chart) with the induced sc-structures stand for $T_xX$, $Y_x$, which carry no linear structure here (G.7). Two steps the text leaves out: that $D(g - s)(0) = \Gamma(0)^{-1}Dh(0)D\psi(0)$, the conjugate of the basic germ's linearization, is sc-Fredholm (the criterion of V1.8: $\Gamma(0)$ preserves the levels and $Dh(0)$ is regularizing), and the sc-structures of $T_0O$, $K_0$ (Definition 2.47 at the smooth point $0$, the closed graph theorem). No tameness is assumed. In other charts the levels are transported by the chart change at smooth points (Findings, Chapter 3, items 235, 239). Formerly level $0$ only (G.22, Findings item 48); updated in the third addendum of this page.

The first formal statement (`proposition_3_52`, kept for the theorems that use it) gives the index as “$n - N$ for some $n, N \in \mathbb N$”, which every integer satisfies. `proposition_3_52_index` names the conjugation data and identifies $n$, $N$ with the dimensions of the conjugating basic germ, for every conjugation (Findings, Chapter 3, item 120). Updated after the first edition of this page.
In every other strong bundle chart around $x_0$ the linearization is Fredholm of the same index, and onto at a zero in good position (V3.96). Updated in the second addendum of this page.

**Germs.** The hypothesis is the text’s since the switch to the germ reading (phase 2): an sc-Fredholm germ whose filling and sc$^+$-section are germs whose levels may shrink with $m$ (V3.13); $Dg(0)$ is the value at $0$ of a derivative family of the filling germ, the same for every family on every germ. The forms for germ data on the whole chart are the `_wholeChart` declarations of the same names (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 289, 310, 331). Hence “restated” (formerly “narrower”, for that hypothesis): what remains is the reading in charts.

items.title: Definition 3.53: good position of an sc-Fredholm germ

book.label: §3.6, Definition 3.53, p. 111
book.statement: An sc-Fredholm germ $(f, x)$ of a tame strong bundle with $f(x) = 0$ is in good position if (1) $f'(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ is surjective and (2) if $d_X(x) \ge 1$, $\ker f'(x)$ is in good position to the partial cone $C_xX$ in $T_xX$.

lean.statement: In the chart of Definition 3.11 (`IsGoodPositionAtGerm`, at $Dg(0)$ for a derivative family $Dg$ of the filling germ $g$): $Tf(0) = Dg(0)|_{T_0O} : T_0O \to K_0$ is onto and $\ker Dg(0)$ is in good position to $C_0O = T_0O \cap C$ inside $T_0O$ (`IsInGoodPositionIn`); `IsGoodPositionAt` is the case of a whole-chart filled version. For a section (`StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGerm f x₀`): the data of Definition 3.11 at $x_0$ with the germ in good position in that chart. With the text’s sc-complement (`IsGoodPositionAtScGerm`; for a section `StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermSc`, in a tame chart): the kernel has a good sc-complement inside $T_0O$ ($T_m = N_m \oplus P_m$ on every level). At a zero of an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data the two forms agree.

chips: sc-complement form: the same at zeros
diff: Stated in a chart centred at $x$, not in $T_xX$ (the transport of $C_xX$ to $T_xX$ is not formalized, Chapter 2 gap). The case distinction $d_X(x) \ge 1$ is dropped: at an interior point (2) holds trivially (Findings, Chapter 3, item 50), and for tame germ data good position in a tame chart at a zero with $d_X = 0$ is the surjectivity of the linearization (V3.100).

At a zero, the linearization and the two conditions do not depend on the chart (V3.78); Definition 3.53 at a zero from a chart not centred there is V3.79, in any chart of the germ data V3.107. The form in a tame chart (`StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermTame`), which the theorems of §3.6 assume and conclude, is V3.103.

The sc form needs the kernel smooth and a closed good complement in $E$. At a zero $\ker Dg(0)$ is the image under $D\psi'(0)$ of the basic germ's smooth kernel, and the good position of the kernel in $E$ comes from the transport from $T_0O$, so V3.20 applies (Findings, Chapter 3, item 212). “$T = N \oplus P$ an sc-splitting of $T$” is written in $E$; its equivalence with an sc-splitting of the sc-Banach space $T_0O$ is not formalized, nor is the upgrade from good position inside $T$ alone (items 211, 214). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

**Germs.** Since the switch to the text’s germ reading (phase 2) the germ data are the text’s (V3.13), and the condition in the chart is read at $Dg(0)$, the value at $0$ of any derivative family of the filling germ (the same for all, `IsGoodPositionGerm.forall_isGoodPositionAtGerm`); the whole-chart forms are `IsGoodPositionGermWholeChart`, `IsGoodPositionGermScWholeChart` (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 280, 320, 330).

items.title: Theorem 3.54: the solution set as a graph (part (3) of the proof)

book.label: §3.6, Theorem 3.54, p. 111 (proof pp. 111–115)
book.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section of a tame strong bundle with $f(x) = 0$ and $(f, x)$ in good position. The dimension $d$ is existentially quantified here; “the dimension agrees with the Fredholm index” is V3.97 and “$\ker f'(y) = T_yS$” in the chart V3.99. The proof is Theorem 3.23 (V3.69) and Lemma 2.26, $d_S \le d_X = 0$. Added after the first edition of this page; updated in the second addendum of this page.

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).

The first clause, “$f'(x_0)$ is sc-Fredholm”, is proved on every level: in the chart at $x_0$ by Propositions 3.10, 1.10 and 3.5 in sc form, and $Tf(x_0)$ is onto on every level because it is onto on level $0$ and regularizing (Findings, Chapter 3, items 235, 236); formerly level $0$ only. Updated in the third addendum of this page. The section-level sc form `theorem_3_19_linearization_sc` takes the text's sc-Fredholm section (germ reading). The clause with no chart singled out: in every strong bundle chart around $x_0$, $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z$ is an sc-Fredholm operator with the same index on every level (`StrongBundle.linAt_isScFredholm`, V3.96); cited here since the fifth addendum of this page.

items.title: Theorem 3.23: the implicit function theorem, boundary case

book.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.23, p. 77
book.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section of a tame strong bundle, $f(x) = 0$, $f'(x)$ surjective with kernel in good position to $C_xX$. Then there is an open $U \ni x$ such that $S(f, U)$ consists of smooth points and is a tame sub-M-polyfold of $X$, with a uniquely determined structure of a smooth manifold with boundary with corners, the induced one of Proposition 2.21.

lean.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section, $f(x) = 0$, $(f, x)$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103), and let every zero in an open $V_{x_0} \ni x$ be in good position in a tame chart. Then there are an open $U$, $x \in U \subseteq V_{x_0}$, and $d \in \mathbb N$ such that every zero in $U$ is a smooth point and $S(f, U)$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure (Proposition 2.21) is tame and equivalent to that of a $d$-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners. `theorem_3_23`: the same for tame germ data under `IsGoodPositionGermFilled` at $x$ (V3.82) instead of the nearby good position, and then every zero in $U$ is in good position in a tame chart.

diff: Hypotheses of these two forms: the good position of the zeros near $x$ (which is Theorem 3.54 (1), now a theorem, V3.94), or the filler condition at the nearby zeros (V3.82, a consequence of good position, V3.102). The form with the text's hypotheses is V3.95, with the dimension as the Fredholm index V3.97 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 153, 155, 170, 180).

Tameness of the bundle is read as Definitions 3.50, 3.51, 3.53 read it: germ data and good position in tame charts (V3.103). The dimension $d$ is existentially quantified; the identification $d = \dim\ker f'(x)$ is in the proof. “Uniquely determined” is the equivalence of the atlas of the charts $\pi\varphi$ with the induced one, not stated separately. Added after the first edition of this page; updated in the second addendum of this page.

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).

items.title: Corollary 3.24: the solution set when every zero is in good position

book.label: §3.1, Corollary 3.24, p. 78
book.statement: If at every zero $x$ of the sc-Fredholm section $f$ of a tame strong bundle $f'(x)$ is surjective with kernel in good position to $C_xX$, then the solution set $S = \{f = 0\}$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame and that of a smooth manifold with boundary with corners.

lean.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section with $(f, x)$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103) at every zero $x$, and $S = \{f = 0\} \ne \emptyset$. Then $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $X$ whose induced structure is tame and equivalent to a manifold with boundary with corners of locally constant dimension (`IsManifoldWithCornersLoc`, V3.72). The same with good position in the text's sense (sc-complement, V3.47) at every zero, which for an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data is the same hypothesis (`corollary_3_24_sc`).

diff: **No hypothesis is added** (Findings, Chapter 3, items 156, 157): the global hypothesis, good position at every zero, supplies at every point the nearby good position that the local theorems need. “Tame strong bundle” is read as Definitions 3.50, 3.53 read it, good position in a tame chart (V3.103); $S \ne \emptyset$ is needed by the formal charts (for $S = \emptyset$ the statement is empty). The text names no dimension; the formal one is locally constant (V3.87). Added after the first edition of this page.

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).

Corollary 3.24 with the text's notion of good position is `corollary_3_24_sc`; for an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data that hypothesis is equivalent to the project's (`forall_isGoodPositionGermSc_iff`; Findings, Chapter 3, item 213). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Tameness is carried by sc-diffeomorphisms and by open subsets

book.label: §3.2, proof of Proposition 3.26, p. 80; §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.54, p. 114
book.statement: Used without statement: in the proof of Proposition 3.26, “$X' = \psi(X)$ is tame”; in the proof of Theorem 3.54, the chart $\psi \circ \varphi$ onto $\psi(O)$ is a chart of the tame M-polyfold $X$.

lean.statement: For an sc-diffeomorphism $\psi : U \to U'$ between relatively open subsets of partial quadrants and a tame retraction $r : U \to U$ onto $O$, $\psi \circ r \circ \psi^{-1}$ is a tame retraction of $U'$ onto $\psi(O)$, so $(\psi(O), C', E')$ is a tame retract; on the way $d_{C'} \circ \psi = d_C$, $Dr'(\psi(x)) = D\psi(x)Dr(x)D\psi^{-1}(\psi(x))$, and sc-isomorphisms carry sc-subspaces and sc-splittings. The restriction of a tame retraction to an open subset is tame; an open subset of a tame retract, and the model of a chart restricted to an open set, are tame retracts.

diff: Condition (1) of Definition 2.34 is Theorem 1.25; condition (2) is transported at the smooth points, where $D\psi(x)$ is an sc-isomorphism, using $D\psi(x)E_x \subseteq E'_{\psi(x)}$ (the one-sided sign argument) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 95, 151). Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: Theorem 3.27 with locally constant dimension

book.label: §3.2, Theorem 3.27, p. 81
book.statement: Theorem 3.27 for a fixed dimension $n$: a subset with the $n$-dimensional tangent germ property is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame and equivalent to an $n$-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners, with the charts $\pi \circ \varphi$.

lean.statement: If $M \ne \emptyset$ has at every point regular data of Definition 3.25 (`IsRegular`, V3.24) of some dimension, which may depend on the point, then $M$ is a sub-M-polyfold, its induced structure is tame, and the charts $\pi\varphi$ of all these data form an equivalent atlas of charts on relatively open subsets of partial quadrants of finite-dimensional spaces (`IsManifoldWithCornersLoc`); each of them is a chart of the induced structure containing its point.

diff: The regularity conditions of V3.24 are hypotheses, as there. The dimension may vary from point to point (the solution set of Theorem 3.57 has locally constant, not constant, dimension; Findings, Chapter 3, item 152); the proof is that of V3.24. Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: The re-centring lemma

book.label: §3.2, proof of Theorem 3.27, p. 84
book.statement: In the proof of Theorem 3.27: $\delta$ is an sc$^\infty$-germ near every $v_0 \in V$. With the data $(\psi, N', Y', V', \tau)$ at $x_0 = \varphi^{-1}(v_0 + \delta(v_0))$, the map $w \mapsto \pi\varphi\psi^{-1}(w + \tau(w))$ has an invertible linearization at $0$, so it is a local diffeomorphism and $\delta$ is regular near $v_0$.

lean.statement: For two graph descriptions of one set $S$ — in a chart $\chi_1$ the graph of $\sigma_1 : V_1 \to Y_1$ over $K_1$ with $\sigma_1$ of class $C^1$ on all of $V_1$, in a chart $\chi_2$ centred at $y = \chi_1^{-1}(v_0 + \sigma_1(v_0))$ the graph of $\sigma_2$ over $K_2$ with $\sigma_2(0) = 0$, $D\sigma_2(0) = 0$ and $C^k$-lifts into level $k$ near $0$ ($K_i$ finite-dimensional, smooth, in good position, $Y_i$ closed complements) — $\dim K_1 = \dim K_2$, and for all $m$, $k$, $\sigma_1$ is $C^k$ into $E_{1,m}$ on a relatively open neighbourhood of $v_0$.

chips: onto by Sard, not by symmetry
diff: The text's step needs $\delta$ differentiable at $v_0$, which fails for general sets (V3.24, first counterexample); here $\sigma_1$ is $C^1$ on $V_1$, which V3.74 arranges by shrinking (Findings, Chapter 3, items 82, 150).

The linearization of $\beta = \pi_1 \circ \chi_1\chi_2^{-1} \circ (1 + \sigma_2)$ at $0$ is injective by the chain rule for the transition and its inverse on level $1$ and the tangency of the graph to the retract; its surjectivity comes from the dimension count by Sard's lemma in fixed dimension, since the symmetric argument would need $\sigma_1$ differentiable into level $1$ at $v_0$ (item 159). The inverse $\beta^{-1}$ is $C^k$ by Lemma 3.77 with weak hypotheses (V3.90), not by Theorem 3.72, which would need $d_C(x) = d_C(\beta(x))$. Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: Condition (a) of the regularity conditions by re-centring

book.label: §3.2, proof of Theorem 3.27, p. 84; §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.54, p. 115
book.statement: The proof of Theorem 3.27 shows that $\delta$ is an sc$^\infty$-germ near every point of $V$ (so that the charts $\pi\varphi$ are compatible); the proof of Theorem 3.54 constructs the data at every zero “proceeding as above”.

lean.statement: Let $D$ be data of Definition 3.25 of dimension $n$ for $M$ at $x$ with $\pi(O) \subseteq C$ (condition (b)), and let every point of $M$ in an open $U \ni x$ have data of Definition 3.25 of some dimension. Then $M$ has at $x$ regular data (`IsRegular`) of dimension $n$ with chart domain in $U$, and every datum of Definition 3.25 at a point of $M$ in that domain has dimension $n$. (The proof shrinks $D$ — same $N$, $Y$, $\delta$ — and applies V3.73 at every point.)

diff: Condition (b), $\pi(O) \subseteq C$, is a hypothesis. Read off the statement (not a separate Lean theorem): every point of a set with the tangent germ property has data, so for such a set data satisfying (b) can be shrunk to regular data; condition (a) of V3.24 is then not an independent hypothesis. For the solution set (b) holds by the choice of the good complement (V3.75, V3.77; Findings, Chapter 3, items 151, 152). Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: Good complements whose projection maps the partial quadrant into itself

book.label: §3.2, proof of Theorem 3.27, p. 83
book.statement: In the proof of Theorem 3.27 the set $\Sigma = \{v + y \in C \mid v \in V, y \in Y\}$ is asserted to be relatively open in $C$; the retraction $t(v + w) = v + \delta(v)$ is defined on it.

lean.statement: If the finite-dimensional $N$ is in good position to the partial quadrant $C$ of $E$, there is a continuous projection $\pi : E_0 \to N$ with $\pi(C) \subseteq N \cap C$ whose kernel $Y$ is a good complement of $N$; $Y$ is closed and `ProjectsInto C N Y` ($z \in C$, $k \in N$, $z - k \in Y$ imply $k \in C$). The property is carried by continuous linear isomorphisms respecting the cones.

chips: a case the obvious choice misses
diff: The text's claim fails for an arbitrary good complement (V3.24, second counterexample) and holds when $\pi(O) \subseteq C$; for the solution set the complement is chosen so (V3.77). The construction keeps the coordinates of a set $S$ of indices; when no coordinate vanishes at a nonzero point of $N \cap C$ and $N \cap C \ne N$ one coordinate is kept: for $C = [0, \infty)^2$, $N = \mathbb R(1, 1)$ the projection along the good complement $\mathbb R(1, 2)$ maps $(0, 1)$ to $-(1, 1)$ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 130, 131). Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: Corollary 3.39: composition with a given conjugation

book.label: §3.4, Corollary 3.39, p. 93
book.statement: If the sc-germ $g$ is equivalent by a strong bundle isomorphism $\Phi$ to a basic germ and $s$ is an sc$^+$-germ, there is a strong bundle map $\Psi$ such that $((\Psi \circ \Phi)_*(g + s))^1$ is a basic germ.

lean.statement: Let $g : U \to F$ be sc-smooth and conjugated to a basic germ $h$ (conjugation data $\Phi$, V3.13, V3.46), and $s : U \to F_1$ sc-smooth into $F^1$ with $s(0) = 0$. With $t = \Phi[1]_*s$ and $h' = h + (t_{\mathbb R^N}, 0)$ there are data of Theorem 3.38 for $t_W$ such that $\Phi_*(g + s) = h + t$ near $0$, $\Gamma = \Lambda \circ \Phi^1$ is a strong bundle isomorphism of the shifted structures $E^1 \triangleleft F^1$ with $\Gamma_* = \Lambda_* \circ \Phi^1_*$, and $(\Gamma(u, (g + s)^1(u)))_2 = (\Lambda_*(h + t))^1(\gamma(u))$ near $0$, a basic germ; so $(g + s)^1$ is conjugated to a basic germ. Also $\Gamma = (\Lambda_0 \circ \Phi)^1$.

chips: index raise of an iso: proved
diff: “Sc-germ” is read as sc-smooth on $U$ and the sc$^+$-germ $s$ as an sc-smooth map into $F^1$ on $U$ with $s(0) = 0$; the conclusion is a conjugation of the level-$1$ map $(g + s)^1$ on the shifted structures. The text's “strong bundle map $\Psi$” is an isomorphism (the linear change of Theorem 3.38); the index raise of a strong bundle isomorphism is one (used silently by the text); $\Phi_*(g + s) = h + t$ holds near $0$ only, with the $\mathbb R^N$-component of $t$ absorbed into $h$; the text's $\tau : Z \to C$ is not applied (Findings, Chapter 3, items 121–123). Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: Theorems 3.43, 3.47 and 3.54 (3) with a closed good complement projecting into the quadrant

book.label: §3.5, Theorem 3.43 and Corollary 3.47, pp. 102, 106; §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.54, p. 114
book.statement: Theorem 3.43 and Corollary 3.47 (local solvability) with a good complement $Y$ of the kernel; Theorem 3.54, step (3): the solution set near $x$ is the graph of $\sigma$ over $\ker D(h + t)(0) \cap C'$.

lean.statement: The conclusions of V3.38, V3.42 and V3.48 hold with a good complement $Y$ that is closed and satisfies `ProjectsInto` for the partial quadrant (V3.75). In Theorem 3.43, $Y = Z \oplus W$ for a good complement $Z$ of $\widetilde K$ chosen by V3.75: every good complement $Z$ of $\widetilde K$ gives the good complement $Z \oplus W$ of $K'$ (constant $\varepsilon/(\|L\| + 1)$) and the data of the proof exist for a prescribed $Z$; in Corollary 3.47 both properties are carried by the linear homeomorphism of Theorem 3.38.

diff: Two additional conclusions. The closedness is the text's (its $Y'$ is an sc-complement) and is needed by Lemma 3.55 and Definition 3.25 at the nearby zeros; the projection property is not in the text and gives condition (b) of Theorem 3.27 for the solution set (V3.84; Findings, Chapter 3, items 93, 132, 133). Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: The linearization at a zero in charts, and its chart independence

book.label: §3.6, Definition 3.53, p. 111; §2.4, Definition 2.38, p. 42
book.statement: Definition 3.53 is stated with $f'(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ and the partial cone $C_xX$; Definition 2.38 asserts that $T^R_xX$ and $C_xX$ do not depend on the chart (Proposition 2.30). The linearization is defined at the centre of a chart, through a filler.

lean.statement: In a strong bundle chart, $\mathrm{Lin}(z) = D(\mathbf f \circ r)(z)|_{T_zO}$ at every level-$1$ point $z$ of the retract; at a zero it takes values in $K_z = \rho(z)F$ and equals $Dg(z)$ on $T_zO$ for every $g$ sc$^1$ on $U$ agreeing with $\mathbf f$ near $z$, and for every sc$^1$-germ $g$ agreeing with $\mathbf f$ near $z$ with $z$ in its germ, $Dg(z)$ the value of its derivative family (`linAt_eq_germDeriv`; at a centre: $Tf(0)$ of Proposition 3.5, also for a filling germ). For two strong bundle charts of $P$ and an sc-smooth section, at a zero $y$ with level-$1$ points $z$, $z'$ over $\varphi(y)$, $\varphi'(y)$: isomorphisms $A : T_zO \to T_{z'}O'$, $\Gamma : K_z \to K'_{z'}$ with $\Gamma\,\mathrm{Lin}(z) = \mathrm{Lin}'(z')A$ and $A$ respecting the partial quadrants; so surjectivity, the Fredholm property and index, and the good position of the kernel do not depend on the chart.

diff: The text does not prove the chart independence of $f'(x)$ or of good position; this is its chart form at zeros (what gap G.13 of Chapter 2 leaves open). Only the fibre derivative of the transition survives at a zero, so away from zeros the linearization is not chart independent. Of Definition 2.50 only the sc-smoothness of the transition on $[0]$ is used; level-$1$ points suffice; no tameness (Findings, Chapter 3, items 110–116). Added after the first edition of this page.

For filling germs (the germ reading of Definition 3.11) $Dg(z)$ is meaningful only for $z$ in the germ; the consumers use it at the centre and at the level-$1$ lifts of nearby zeros, which lie in the germ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 278, 284). Updated after the switch of Definition 3.11 to the text’s germ reading (phase 2).

items.title: Definition 3.53 at a zero, from a chart not centred there

book.label: §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.54, p. 115
book.statement: In the proof of Theorem 3.54: at every zero $y$ near $x$, $f'(y)$ is surjective with kernel in good position, “so that, proceeding as above”, the construction can be repeated at $y$.

lean.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-smooth section, $y$ a zero with tame germ data (V3.103), $c$ a strong bundle chart of $P$ around $y$ (not necessarily centred), $z$ a level-$1$ point over $\varphi(y)$, $g$ an sc$^1$-germ on a germ $G$ of $c$ with derivative family $Dg$ and $z \in G_1$, agreeing with $\mathbf f$ on $O$ near $\varphi(y)$. If $\rho(z)k \in Dg(z)(T_zO)$ for every smooth $k$ and $\ker Dg(z) \cap T_zO$ is in good position to $C_{\varphi(y)}$ inside $T_zO$, then $(f, y)$ is in good position in a tame chart (`isGoodPositionGermTame_of_chart_dense`); with all of $K_z$ in the range, for an sc-Fredholm germ, in the chart of Definition 3.11 (`isGoodPositionGerm_of_chart`); the same with the hypotheses on $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ (`isGoodPositionGerm_of_linAt_surj`).

diff: The hypothesis is on $\ker Dg(z) \cap T_zO$, not on $\ker Dg(z)$: condition (3) of the filler holds at its centre only, so $\ker Dg(z)$ need not lie in $T_zO$. A dense part of $K_z$ in the range suffices because the range of the linearization in the centred chart is closed (Proposition 3.52) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 111, 117). Added after the first edition of this page.

In the germ reading of Definition 3.11 the point $z$ must lie in the germ of $g$; the dense form needs the closed range in the target chart, which Proposition 3.52 for germs gives in the tame chart of the germ data, so it is stated there. The whole-chart forms are `isGoodPositionGerm_of_chart_dense`, `isGoodPositionGerm_of_linAt` and the `_wholeChart` declarations (Findings, Chapter 3, items 285, 301, 313). Updated after the switch of Definition 3.11 to the text’s germ reading (phase 2).

items.title: Theorem 3.54, property (4) in the chart at $x_0$: Corollary 3.41 and Lemma 3.55 on the graph

book.label: §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.54, property (4), and Lemma 3.55, p. 114
book.statement: For every zero $y \in V$, with $\psi\varphi(y) = v + \sigma(v)$, the kernel of $f'(y)$ is in good position and $f'(y)$ is surjective; this follows from Corollary 3.41 and Lemma 3.55.

lean.statement: In the data of V3.48 (a section, $(f, x_0)$ in good position in a tame chart) there are a presentation $T$ of $C'$ and an open $V_{x,1} \ni x_0$ such that for every zero $y \in V_{x,1}$ with $\psi\varphi(y) = v + \sigma(v)$: $v + \sigma(v)$ lies on level $1$ and $D(h + t)$ there is surjective Fredholm of index $n - N$; $v + \sigma(v) \in C'$; and $Y$ is a good complement of $N_v = \{k + D\sigma(v)k\}$ with respect to $C'_{v + \sigma(v)}$, with $N_v$ in good position. Lemma 3.55 for $\sigma$ on a relatively open $V \subseteq N \cap C$, any presentation of $C$, closed $Y$.

diff: A step of the proof: in the chart at $x_0$ and for the tangent space $N_v$ of the graph; its identification with the kernel at $y$ is V3.81, the passage to Definition 3.53 at $y$ is V3.79, V3.82. Lemma 3.55 is applied to $\sigma$ on a relatively open $V'$, extended to the cone by a bump; that $N_v \cap C_z$ has interior in $N_v$, which Lemma 3.55 does not state, holds once $\|D\sigma(v)\|$ is small (Findings, Chapter 3, items 91, 92). Added after the first edition of this page.

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).

items.title: Theorem 3.54 (1) at the nearby zeros: the kernel

book.label: §3.6, Theorem 3.54 (1), the kernel, pp. 111, 114
book.statement: At every zero $y$ near $x$, $\ker f'(y)$ is in good position to the partial cone $C_yX$ (from Corollary 3.41 and Lemma 3.55).

lean.statement: For a section $f$ of a strong bundle, $f(x_0) = 0$ and $(f, x_0)$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103): in a tame chart centred at $x_0$ (filling germ $g$ with a derivative family $Dg$, conjugation covering $\psi$, the germ $h + t$ with kernel $K$, graph $\sigma$) there is an open $V_{x,2} \ni x_0$ such that at every zero $y \in V_{x,2}$, $z_0 = \varphi(y)$, whose level-$1$ lift lies in the germ of $g$: $N_v = \ker D(h + t)$ at $v + \sigma(v) = \psi(z_0)$; $\ker Dg(z_0) = D\psi^{-1}(N_v)$; $Dg(z_0)$ is onto; $\ker Dg(z_0) \subseteq T_{z_0}O$; and $\ker Dg(z_0)$ is in good position to $C_{z_0}$ inside $T_{z_0}O$.

diff: The kernel half of (1), in the chart at $x_0$, with the text's hypotheses. Two steps the text does not mention: $N_v \subseteq \ker D(h + t)$ needs the $C^1$-lift of $\sigma$ into level $1$ (Theorem 3.47 (1)), equality follows from a dimension count; and $\ker Dg(z_0) \subseteq T_{z_0}O$ comes from the tangency of the solution set to $O$, not from the filler, whose condition (3) holds at $0$ only (Findings, Chapter 3, items 101–104). The surjectivity half is V3.93. Added after the first edition of this page.

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).

In the germ reading the level-$1$ lift of $z_0$ lies in the germ of the filling because the basic germ is taken on the points that $\psi^{-1}$ maps into the germs of $g$ and $s$ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 276–278, 295). Updated after the switch of Definition 3.11 to the text’s germ reading (phase 2).

items.title: Theorem 3.54 (1) under the filler condition at the nearby zeros (first form)

book.label: §3.6, Theorem 3.54 (1), p. 111 (proof p. 114)
book.statement: At every zero $y$ near $x$, the sc-Fredholm germ $(f, y)$ is in good position: $f'(y)$ is surjective and its kernel is in good position (from Corollary 3.41 and Lemma 3.55).

lean.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (V3.103), $f(x_0) = 0$, and $(f, x_0)$ in good position in a tame chart **with a filler $g$ that satisfies condition (3) of Definition 3.4 at its zeros near $0$** (`IsGoodPositionGermFilled`: at every level-$1$ zero $z_1$ of $g$ in $O \cap N$ lying in the germ of $g$, for its derivative family $Dg$, $Dr(z_1)b = 0$ and $\rho(z_1)Dg(z_1)b = Dg(z_1)b$ imply $b = 0$). Then there is an open $V_x \ni x_0$ such that $(f, y)$ is in good position in a tame chart at every zero $y \in V_x$. Step: at a zero $z$ with $Dg(z)$ onto and condition (3) at $z$, $\rho(z)F \subseteq Dg(z)(T_zO)$.

diff: **The hypothesis of this form.** Definition 3.4 imposes condition (3) at $0$ only, and the text's argument does not give the surjectivity of $f'(y)$: in the block form of $Dg(z_0)$ with respect to $T_{z_0}O \oplus \ker Dr(z_0)$ and $K_{z_0} \oplus \ker\rho(z_0)$, $Tf(z_0)$ is onto iff the block $(1 - \rho(z_0))Dg(z_0)|_{\ker Dr(z_0)}$ is injective, i.e. iff the index is locally constant along the solution set; both directions are formalized (V3.102). The same step is in the book's arXiv version (Theorem 3.13 there). items.title: Theorem 3.54 (1)–(2): good position near $x_0$ and the regular tangent germ data

items.title: Theorem 3.56: the global implicit function theorem, $\partial X = \emptyset$

book.label: §3.6, Theorem 3.56, p. 115
book.statement: If $P : Y \to X$ is a tame strong bundle over an M-polyfold with $\partial X = \emptyset$ and $f$ an sc-Fredholm section with surjective linearization at every point of $S = \{f = 0\}$, then $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is equivalent to a smooth manifold without boundary.

items.title: Theorem 3.57: the global implicit function theorem, boundary case

book.label: §3.6, Theorem 3.57, p. 115
book.statement: If $P : Y \to X$ is a tame strong bundle and $f$ an sc-Fredholm section such that at every $x \in S = \{f = 0\}$ the linearization is surjective with kernel in good position to $C_xX$, then $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame and equivalent to a smooth manifold with boundary with corners.

items.title: Theorem 3.58, given the family of sc-isomorphisms

book.label: §3.7, proof of Theorem 3.58, pp. 118–120
book.statement: Second half of the proof of Theorem 3.58: with $L(b) = P_Y \circ Df(b)|_X$ sc-isomorphisms with uniform lower bounds (Lemmas 3.59–3.61), the strong bundle isomorphism $\Phi((b, x), (c, y)) = ((b, x), (c, L(b)^{-1}y))$ makes $\Phi_*(f - f(0))$ a basic germ, the contraction estimate coming from condition (3).

lean.statement: In coordinates $E = \mathbb R^n \oplus X$, $C = \widetilde C \oplus X$, $F = \mathbb R^N \oplus Y$: for $f$ sc-smooth on $U$, an open $V_o \ni 0$ with $(b, 0) \in U$ for $b \in V_o \cap \widetilde C$, sc-isomorphisms $L(b)$ with $L(b)h = (Df(b, 0)(0, h))_Y$ and lower bounds $c_m$ on $V_o \cap \widetilde C$, and condition (3) (`DerivCondition`): on $U' = U \cap (V_o \oplus X)$ the push-forward $k = \Phi_*(f - f(0))$ is a basic germ with contraction $H(b, x) = x - L(b)^{-1}(f(b, x) - f(0))_Y$, $\Phi$ is a strong bundle isomorphism covering the identity, and $f - f(0)$ is conjugated to a basic germ.

chips: in the coordinates of the proof

The contraction estimate uses the mean value inequality along a segment with the derivative bound in the weaker norm of $X_m$ (the text's integral formula), first for $x, x' \in X_{m+1}$, then by density; the sc-smoothness of $(b, y) \mapsto L(b)^{-1}y$ is Lemma 3.61 in set form (Findings, Chapter 3, item 73). items.title: Theorem 3.58: the basic germ criterion

book.label: §3.7, Theorem 3.58, p. 116 (proof pp. 116–120)
book.statement: Under (1) $Df(x)$ sc-Fredholm of constant index at smooth points, (2) a splitting $E = B \oplus X$ with $B \supseteq \ker Df(0)$, $Y = Df(0)X$ and a compactness condition, (3) a uniform estimate on $D_2f$: $f - f(0)$ is conjugated near $0$ to a basic germ.

lean.statement: In coordinates $E = \mathbb R^n \oplus X$, $C = \widetilde C \oplus X$, $F = \mathbb R^N \oplus Y$: let $f$ be sc-smooth on $U$ with (1) $Df(b, 0)$ sc-Fredholm with the sc-index of $Df(0)$ at every $(b, 0) \in U$, $b \in \widetilde C$; (2) $h \mapsto (Df(0)(0, h))_Y$ bijective on level $0$ and `CompactnessCondition`; (3) `DerivCondition`. Then there are an open $V_o \ni 0$ and sc-isomorphisms $L(b) = P_Y Df(b, 0)|_X$ for $b \in V_o \cap \widetilde C$ with the conclusions of V3.88: $f - f(0)$ is conjugated to a basic germ.

chips: in the coordinates of the proof

items.title: Proposition 3.73 and Lemma 3.77 with the hypotheses their proofs use

book.label: §3.8.4, Proposition 3.73 and Lemma 3.77, pp. 137, 140
book.statement: For $U$ relatively open and convex in a partial quadrant $C \subseteq \mathbb R^n$, $f : U \to C$ smooth with $\|Df - 1\| \le \tfrac12$, $f(0) = 0$ and $d_C(x) = d_C(f(x))$: $f(U)$ is relatively open and $f : U \to f(U)$ is a smooth diffeomorphism (Lemma 3.77: the inverse is differentiable with $Dg = [Df \circ g]^{-1}$).

items.title: Theorem 3.18: parametrized perturbations

book.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.18, p. 74
book.statement: Let $P : Y \to X$ be a tame strong bundle and $f$ an sc-Fredholm section. If $s_1, \dots, s_n \in \Gamma^+(P)$, then $(r, x) \mapsto f(x) + \sum_i r_is_i(x)$ defines an sc-Fredholm section of the pull-back bundle $\pi^*(P) : \pi^*Y \to \mathbb R^n \times X$.

lean.statement: For any strong bundle $P : Y \to X$, an sc-Fredholm section $f$ and sc$^+$-sections $s_1, \dots, s_n$: with $\mathbb R^n$ the M-polyfold with the constant sc-structure and the translation charts, $\pi(r, x) = x$, and $\pi^*P$ the pull-back strong bundle with the natural structure of Proposition 2.54, $F(r, x) = f(x) + \sum_i r_is_i(x)$ (computed in $P^{-1}(x)$) is an sc-Fredholm section of $\pi^*P$. The paracompactness of $\mathbb R^n \times X$ and $\pi^*Y$ is supplied by Theorem 2.16 (`theorem_3_18'`). On the way: $\tilde f = f \circ \pi$ is sc-Fredholm (product chart, the $\mathbb R^n$-extension of the basic germ), $\tilde s$ is sc$^+$ (scalar product rule), $F = \tilde f + \tilde s$, Theorem 3.15; $\mathbb R^n \times X$ is tame when $X$ is.

diff: Tameness is not used, as for Theorem 3.15; $\pi^*P$ is tame when $P$ is. The text's “readily verified” needs objects it does not construct: $\mathbb R^n$ as an M-polyfold with charts centred at every $r_0$, the product chart pulled back to $\pi^*Y$, the filler conditions for $(a, u) \mapsto g(u)$, and the $\mathbb R^n$-extension of the basic germ; that $\tilde s$ is sc$^+$ needs the product rule with a scalar factor, which Chapter 1 does not state (Findings, Chapter 3, items 160–164, 167). Added in the second addendum of this page.

items.title: The linearization of the parametrized section

book.label: §3.1, after Theorem 3.19, p. 75
book.statement: The linearization of $\tilde f(r, x) = f(x) + \sum_i r_is_i(x)$ at $(0, x_0)$ is $(h, u) \mapsto f'(x_0)u + \sum_i h_ie_i$, $e_i = s_i(x_0)$.

lean.statement: In the product chart $(r \mapsto r - r_0) \times c$ of $\pi^*P$, $c$ a strong bundle chart of $P$ with $0$ in its retract, at the centre: $D(\hat F \circ (1 \times r))(0)(\delta a, \delta u) = D(\hat G \circ r)(0)\delta u + \sum_i\delta a_i\hat s_i(0)$, $\hat G = \hat f + \sum_i r_{0,i}\hat s_i$; in the chart form of the linearization, $\mathrm{Lin}_F(0)(\delta a, \delta u) = \mathrm{Lin}_{f + \sum r_{0,i}s_i}(0)\delta u + \sum_i\delta a_i\hat s_i(0)$, and at $r_0 = 0$, $\mathrm{Lin}_F(0)(\delta r, \xi) = \mathrm{Lin}_f(0)\xi + \sum_i\delta r_i\hat s_i(0)$.

diff: Stated in the chart form of the linearization (Definition 3.53 is formalized in charts). At $(r_0, x)$ with $r_0 \ne 0$ the first term is the linearization of $f + \sum r_{0,i}s_i$, not $f'(x)$; the formula does not use $F(r_0, x) = 0$. items.title: Theorem 3.54 (1): the surjectivity at the nearby zeros, in the chart at $x_0$

book.label: §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.54, property (4), p. 114
book.statement: For every zero $y$ near $x$ the linearization $f'(y)$ is surjective; “property (4) follows from Corollary 3.41 and from Lemma 3.55”.

lean.statement: In the data of V3.48 at a zero $x_0$ in good position (chart centred at $x_0$, filling germ $g$, conjugation $\Psi$ covering $\psi$, $h' + \iota t$ with kernel $K \ne 0$, the graph $\sigma$ over $V'$, an open $N_2 \ni 0$ on which $\psi$ maps the zeros of $g$ in $O$ onto the graph), with condition (2) of Definition 3.4 on $N_2$: there is an open $N_4 \subseteq N_2$ containing $0$ such that for every zero $z_0 \in O \cap N_4$ of $g$ and every smooth $k$, $\rho(z_0)k = Dg(z_0)x$ for some $x \in T_{z_0}O$.
